   </ix:exclude>
   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Recognize revenue when or as the Company satisfies a performance obligation</i>. The Company satisfies its performance obligations by transferring a product or service either at a point in time or over time, when the transfer of control of the underlying performance obligation has occurred. Control is evidenced by the customer&#8217;s ability to direct the use of and obtain substantially all the remaining benefits from the performance obligation. Revenue from <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party sales for which the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the criteria for gross revenue recognition is recognized on a net basis. All other revenue is recognized on a gross basis. The Company excludes from the transaction price all sales taxes assessed by governmental authorities and as a result, revenue is presented net of tax.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">As a result of applying this <em style="font: inherit;">five</em>-step model under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> the Company recognizes revenues from its sale of products and services as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Products:</i>&#160;Revenue from the sale of standard products is recognized upon their transfer of control to the customer, which is considered complete at either the time of shipment or arrival at destination, based on the agreed upon terms within the contract. The Company&#8217;s payment terms for the sale of standard products are typically <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-09-30_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="azta:StandardPaymentPeriod" id="c138815098" format="ixt-sec:duryear">30</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-09-30_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="azta:StandardPaymentPeriod" id="c138815099" format="ixt-sec:duryear">60</ix:nonNumeric> days.</p> </td></tr>
<tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;">&#160;</td></tr>
<tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">Revenue from the sales of certain products that involve significant customization, which include primarily automated cold sample management systems is recognized over time as the asset created by the Company&#8217;s performance does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have alternative use to the Company and an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date is present. The Company recognizes revenue as work progresses based on a&#160;percentage of actual labor hours incurred on the project to-date and total estimated labor hours expected to be incurred on the project. The selection of the method to measure progress towards completion requires judgment. The Company has concluded that using the percentage of labor hours incurred to estimated labor hours needed to complete the project most appropriately depicts the Company&#8217;s efforts towards satisfaction of the performance obligation. The Company develops profit estimates for long-term contracts based on total revenue expected to be generated from the project and total costs anticipated to be incurred in the project. These estimates are based on a number of factors, including the degree of required product customization and the work required to be able to install the product in the customer&#8217;s existing environment, as well as the Company&#8217;s historical experience, project plans and an assessment of the risks and uncertainties inherent in the contract related to implementation delays or performance issues that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>or <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be within the Company&#8217;s control. The Company estimates a loss on a contract by comparing total estimated contract revenue to the total estimated contract costs and recognizes a loss during the period in which it becomes probable and can be reasonably estimated. The Company reviews profit estimates for long-term contracts during each reporting period and revises the estimate based on changes in circumstances. Revenue for certain arrangements that involve significant product customization but do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> provide the Company with an enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date are recognized at a point in time, upon completion or substantial completion of the project, provided transfer of control has occurred. The project is considered substantially complete when the Company receives acceptance from the customer and remaining tasks are perfunctory or inconsequential and in control of the Company. Generally, the terms of long-term contracts provide for progress billings based on completion of milestones or other defined phases of work. In certain instances, payments collected from customers in advance of recognizing the related revenue are recorded and presented as contract liabilities within &#8220;Deferred revenue&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. Additionally, due to certain billing constraints within contracts, the customer <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>retain a portion of the contract price until completion of the contract. In these contracts, an unbilled receivable is recorded when revenue recognized <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>exceed billings, which the Company presents as a contract asset on the balance sheet, which is included within the &#8220;Prepaid expenses and other current assets&#8221; in the&#160;Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Services:</i>&#160;Service revenue is generally recognized ratably over time or on an output method, as the customer simultaneously receives and consumes the benefit of these services as they are performed. Payments related to service-type warranties <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be made up front or proportionally over the contract term. Revenue for sample management and storage are recognized over the period the services are rendered or samples are stored. Revenue from genomic services is recognized over time and is based upon the fact that transfer of control takes place over time as determined using the input method of costs incurred. Payment due or received from the customers prior to rendering the associated services are recorded as a contract liability.</p></td></tr>
</tbody></table></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" name="us-gaap:GovernmentAssistancePolicyTextBlock" id="c138815827" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Government Assistance </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company receives government assistance from various domestic and foreign, local, regional and national governments which vary in size and duration in the form of cash grants or refundable tax credits. The government assistance typically specifies conditions that must be met in order for it to be earned, such as employee retention targets, completion of employee training, or the construction or acquisition of property and equipment and are often time bound. If conditions are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> satisfied or if the duration period for the arrangement is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> met, the government assistance is often subject to reduction, repayment, or termination.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company&#8217;s policy is to recognize a benefit in the Consolidated Statements of Operations in &#8220;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c138815720">Other, net</span>&#8221; over the life of the asset or duration of the program when the Company has reasonable assurance that it will comply with the conditions under the government assistance and the government assistance will be received, refundable tax credits <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also result in a reduction in &#8220;Accrued income taxes payable&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. If government assistance is received or is probable of receipt and the amount is determinable by the Company in advance of completion of the conditions, the government assistance is recognized in &#8220;Accrued expenses and other current liabilities&#8221; or &#8220;Other long-term liabilities&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets, as appropriate.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815107" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GovernmentAssistanceNonoperatingIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of government assistance was recognized in &#8220;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c138815721">Other, net</span>&#8221;&#160;in the&#160;Consolidated Statement of Operations. The Company also received advance cash government assistance of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815108" contextRef="i_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="azta:GovernmentAssistanceAmountAdvanceCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, which was&#160;recognized within &#8220;Other long-term liabilities&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. In fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815110" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GovernmentAssistanceNonoperatingIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.1</ix:nonFraction> million of government assistance was recognized in &#8220;Other, net&#8221;&#160;in the Consolidated Statement of Operations. The Company also received advance cash government assistance in fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815112" contextRef="i_2024-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="azta:GovernmentAssistanceAmountAdvanceCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.4</ix:nonFraction> million is recognized within &#8220;Other long-term liabilities&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" name="us-gaap:ResearchAndDevelopmentExpensePolicy" id="c138815828" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Research and Development Expense</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Research and development costs are expensed as incurred. Research and development costs consist primarily of personnel expenses related to development of new products, as well as enhancements and engineering changes to existing products and development of hardware and software components.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" name="azta:RestructuringChargesPolicyTextBlock" id="c138815829" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Restructuring Charges</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Accounting for the timing and amount of termination benefits provided by the Company to employees is determined based on whether: (a) the Company has a substantive plan to provide such benefits, (b) the Company has a written employment contract with the affected employees that includes a provision for such benefits, (c) the termination benefits are due to the occurrence of an event specified in an existing plan or agreement, or (d) the termination benefits are a <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-time benefit. In certain circumstances, employee termination benefits <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>meet more than <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of the characteristics listed above and therefore, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have individual elements that are subject to different accounting models.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">From time to time when executing a restructuring or exit plan, the Company also incurs costs other than termination benefits, such as impairments of long-lived assts that are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer used in operations (including ROU&#160;assets, facility-related property and equipment) and termination costs or penalties to cancel a contractual obligation. Such costs are recognized when incurred, which generally occurs at the contract termination or over the period from when a plan to abandon a leased facility is approved through the cease-use date but charges <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>continue over the remainder of the original contractual period.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c138815830" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Stock-Based Compensation </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The fair value of restricted stock units is determined based on the number of shares granted and the closing price of the Company&#8217;s common stock quoted on the Nasdaq Stock Market on the date of grant. For awards that vest based on service conditions, the Company recognizes stock-based compensation expense on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period. For awards that vest subject to performance conditions, the Company recognizes stock-based compensation expense ratably over the performance period if it is probable that performance condition will be met and adjusts for the percentage of shares probable of achieving the performance goals. Each quarter, management assesses the probability of achieving the performance goals. The Company makes estimates of stock award forfeitures and the number of awards expected to vest. The Company considers many factors in developing forfeiture estimates, including award types, employee classes and historical experience. Current estimates <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>differ from actual results and future changes in estimates.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024,&#160;</em>the Company issued restricted stock unit awards with vesting based on market conditions, which will vest based on achievement of the Company's&#160;relative total shareholder return against the defined peer group&#160;over a&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year period. The fair values for those grants that include vesting based on market conditions are estimated using the Monte Carlo simulation model.&#160;The key assumptions used in the Monte Carlo simulation included (i) the expected volatility based on the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year daily historical volatility as measured on the grant date, (ii) risk-free interest rate based on U.S. Treasury constant maturities yields&#160;as of the grant date, (iii) correlation assumption based on daily share price changes over&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;years between the Company and the peer companies measured on the grant date, and (iv)&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;expected dividend yield.&#160;The compensation cost is recognized ratably over the requisite service period for those grants, which will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be reversed solely because the market condition is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> satisfied.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c138815831" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Income Taxes </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company records income taxes using the asset and liability method. Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax differences between the financial statement carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective income tax bases, as well as operating loss and tax credit carryforwards. The Consolidated Financial Statements contain certain deferred tax assets that were recorded as a result of operating losses, as well as other temporary differences between financial and tax accounting. A valuation allowance is established against deferred tax assets if, based upon the evaluation of positive and negative evidence and the extent to which that evidence is objectively verifiable, it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that some or all of the deferred tax assets will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Significant management judgment is required in determining the Company&#8217;s income tax (benefit) expense, the Company&#8217;s deferred tax assets and liabilities and any valuation allowance recorded against those net deferred tax assets. The Company evaluates the weight of all available evidence to determine whether it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that some portion or all of the net deferred income tax assets will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be realized.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The calculation of the Company&#8217;s income tax liabilities involves consideration of uncertainties in the application of complex tax regulations. The Company recognizes liabilities for uncertain tax positions based on a <em style="font: inherit;">two</em>-step process. The <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> step is to evaluate the tax position for recognition by determining if the weight of available evidence indicates that it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the position will be sustained upon an audit conducted by taxing authorities, including resolution of related appeals or litigation processes, if any. If the Company determines that a tax position will more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be sustained, the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> step requires the Company to estimate and measure the tax benefit as the largest amount that is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be realized upon ultimate settlement. It is inherently difficult and subjective to estimate such amounts, as the Company must determine the probability of various possible outcomes. The Company re-evaluates these uncertain tax positions on a quarterly basis. This evaluation is based on factors, such as changes in facts or circumstances, tax law, new audit activity and effectively settled issues. Determining whether an uncertain tax position is effectively settled requires judgment. A change in recognition or measurement <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>result in the recognition of a tax benefit or an additional charge to the tax expense.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>enter into complex, significant transactions involving mergers, acquisitions and legal entity restructurings that cross multiple tax jurisdictions. Such transactions <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>require the engagement of outside advisors to provide expertise in developing tax positions and opinions on transactions.&#160; These advisors can include tax, legal, accounting and valuation specialists.&#160; All inputs are considered as the Company evaluates the ability to claim tax benefits with regard to such transactions in establishing the proper more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> position noted previously. Even when the Company concludes to meet the more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> standard, risk <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>still exist that the taxing authorities <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>challenge the position, and these risks are greater with greater complexity of the transaction.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">During fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company recorded a $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815136" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="azta:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateReconciliationDeductionWorthlessStockAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">45.6</ix:nonFraction> million benefit for a worthless stock deduction in the United States, which was reflected as a long-term tax receivable on the balance sheet,&#160;net of an unrecognized tax benefit of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815137" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncreasesResultingFromCurrentPeriodTaxPositions" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.5</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160;This transaction involved legal restructuring in foreign jurisdictions and the use of outside specialists. The Company, with the assistance of specialists, evaluated the deduction and believes it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> to be sustained on its technical merits and has recognized&#160;the benefit accordingly in its financial statements.&#160;The tax benefit will result from the carryback of a capital loss, which will be subject to Joint Committee on taxation review due to the amount of the refund claim.&#160;The outcome of such review could&#160;result in a change to the tax benefit that was previously recorded in the financial statements.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c138815832" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Net Income (Loss) per Share</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Basic income or loss per share is determined by dividing net income or loss by the weighted average common shares outstanding during the period. Diluted income or loss per share is determined by dividing net income or loss by diluted weighted average shares outstanding during the period. Diluted weighted average shares reflect the dilutive effect, if any, of potential common shares. To the extent their effect is dilutive, employee equity awards and other commitments to be settled in common stock are included in the calculation of diluted income or loss per share based on the treasury stock method. Potential common shares are excluded from the calculation of dilutive weighted average shares outstanding if their effect would be anti-dilutive at the balance sheet date based on a treasury stock method or due to a net loss.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c138815833" escape="true"><p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Recently Adopted Accounting Pronouncements </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2023, </em>the FASB issued Accounting Standards Update ("ASU") <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">07,</em> <i>Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures</i>. The standard expands reportable segment disclosures by requiring disclosure of significant segment expenses that are regularly provided to the Chief Operating Decision Maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) and included within each reported measure of segment profit or loss, an amount and description of its composition for other segment items, and interim disclosures of a reportable segment&#8217;s profit or loss and assets. The Company adopted the new guidance beginning for fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> Adoption of the new standard did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material impact on the Company's&#160;consolidated results of operations, financial position or cash flows.&#160;The incremental disclosure required under the standard appear in Note <em style="font: inherit;">18,</em> <i>Segment and Geographic Information</i>.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;">2021,</em> the Organization of Economic Cooperation and Development (&#8220;OECD&#8221;) introduced its Pillar II Framework Model Rules (&#8220;Pillar <em style="font: inherit;">2&#8221;</em>), which are designed to impose a <em style="font: inherit;">15%</em> global minimum tax on the earnings of in-scope multinational corporations on a country-by-country basis. Certain aspects of Pillar <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> took effect on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2024 </em>while other aspects went&#160;into effect on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025. </em>The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect the adoption of this standard to have a material impact on its consolidated financial statements as the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect to meet the consolidated revenue threshold of <em style="font: inherit;">&#8364;750</em> million over the next <em style="font: inherit;">twelve</em> months.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b><i>Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> <i>Income Taxes (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>):</i> <i>Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures</i>. The ASU is intended to enhance the transparency and decision usefulness of income tax disclosures primarily through changes to the rate reconciliation and income taxes paid information. This update is effective for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2024, </em>though early adoption is permitted. The Company will adopt this standard in fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2026,</em> which will result in an increase in disclosures required.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em>&#160;<i>Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive Income-Expense Disaggregation Disclosures: Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses.</i>&#160;The ASU requires companies to disaggregate operating expenses into specific categories such as employee compensation, depreciation, and intangible asset amortization, by relevant expense caption on the statement of operations. Additionally, in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2025,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01,</em>&#160;<i>Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income - Expense Disaggregation Disclosures</i>,&#160;to clarify the effective date of ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03.</em>&#160;ASU&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01</em>&#160;is effective for fiscal years beginning after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026,&#160;</em>and interim periods within annual reporting periods beginning after&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027,&#160;</em>on a retrospective or prospective basis, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently evaluating the standard to determine the impact of adoption on its consolidated financial statements and disclosures.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> September 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">06,</em> <i>Intangibles &#8211; Goodwill and Other &#8211; Internal-Use Software (Subtopic <em style="font: inherit;">350</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software.</i>&#160;The ASU simplifies the capitalization guidance by removing all references to software development project stages so that the guidance is neutral to different software development methods. This update is effective for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027. </em>The ASU <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be applied prospectively, retrospectively or using a modified transition approach. The Company is currently evaluating the impact of this ASU on its consolidated financial statements.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;&#160;</p>
  </ix:nonNumeric>
  <div>
   &#160;
  </div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" name="us-gaap:DisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3078619" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b>Discontinued Operations</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Disposition of&#160;B Medical Systems Business</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">first</em>&#160;quarter of fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em>&#160;following approval by the Board of Directors of the Company, the Company publicly announced its plan to sell the B Medical Systems business. The B Medical Systems business operates as a separate business unit within&#160;the Company and focuses&#160;on the manufacturing and distribution of temperature-controlled storage and transportation solutions in international markets to governments, health institutions, and non-government organizations.&#160;This action is intended to simplify the Company's portfolio and allow management to focus on driving revenue growth and profitability in its core businesses. The decision followed&#160;work by the Board of Directors to evaluate strategic, operational and financial opportunities to maximize stockholder value. The Company anticipates entering into a definitive agreement to sell its B Medical Systems business by the end of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company determined that the B Medical Systems business&#160;met the &#8220;held for sale&#8221; criteria and &#8220;discontinued operations&#8221; criteria in accordance with&#160;FASB ASC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">205</em>&#160;as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 12, 2024.&#160;</em>Results related to the B Medical Systems business&#160;are included within discontinued operations. The Consolidated Balance Sheet and Consolidated Statements of Operations, and the notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements, were retroactively reclassified&#160;for all periods presented to reflect the discontinuation of the B Medical Systems business&#160;in accordance with FASB ASC&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">205.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company measured the B Medical Systems business&#160;at the lower of carrying value or fair value less cost to sell at each reporting period. During the fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025,&#160;</em>the Company&#160;recorded $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815175" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsToBeDisposedOf" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">93.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of estimated loss&#160;on assets held for sale based on the estimated fair value of the B Medical Systems business&#160;less costs to sell the business. The fair value is based on&#160;the observable inputs received during the continued progression of the sales process.&#160;The estimated loss&#160;on assets held for sale is included in &#8220;Loss from discontinued operations, net of tax&#8221;&#160;on the Consolidated Statements of Operations for the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025&#160;</em>and&#160;is&#160;included as a valuation allowance or contra-asset account within &#8220;Noncurrent assets held for sale&#8221; on the Consolidated Balance Sheets as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Disposition of Semiconductor&#160;Business</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 1, 2022,&#160;</em>the Company completed the sale of the semiconductor automation business for $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815178" contextRef="d_2022-02-01_2022-02-01_DisposalGroupClassificationAxis-DiscontinuedOperationsDisposedOfBySaleMember_IncomeStatementBalanceSheetAndAdditionalDisclosuresByDisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsAxis-SemiconductorAutomationBusinessMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromDivestitureOfBusinesses" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">2.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;billion in cash to Thomas H. Lee Partners, L.P. On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> July 1, 2019,&#160;</em>the Company completed the sale of the semiconductor cryogenics business for $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815179" contextRef="d_2019-07-01_2019-07-01_DisposalGroupClassificationAxis-DiscontinuedOperationsDisposedOfBySaleMember_IncomeStatementBalanceSheetAndAdditionalDisclosuresByDisposalGroupsIncludingDiscontinuedOperationsAxis-SemiconductorCryogenicsBusinessMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromDivestitureOfBusinesses" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">659.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million to Edwards Vacuum LLC (a member of the Atlas Copco Group) (&#8220;Edwards&#8221;). Both the semiconductor automation business and the semiconductor cryogenics business are considered discontinued operations. In the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>&#160;quarter of fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2020,</em>&#160;Edwards asserted claims for indemnification under the definitive agreement relating to alleged breaches of representations and warranties relating to customer warranty claims and inventory (the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2020</em>&#160;Claim&#8221;). In addition, in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> January 2023,&#160;</em>Edwards filed a lawsuit against the Company in the Supreme Court of the State of New York in the County of New York seeking indemnification from the Company under such definitive agreement for $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815183" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-01-31_LitigationCaseAxis-EdwardsVacuumLlcWarrantyClaimMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and other related damages, including interest and attorney&#8217;s fees, arising from a&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party claim that was included as part of their initial claims (the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2023</em>&#160;Claim&#8221;).</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> April 2023,&#160;</em>the Company responded to and filed a counterclaim against Edwards for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;Claim alleging breach of the definitive agreements by Edwards and seeking a declaratory judgment. Under the settlement agreement, the Company paid Edwards $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815191" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2023-04-30_LitigationCaseAxis-EdwardsVacuumLlcWarrantyClaimMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualPayments" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.8</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million from&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;of the indemnification escrows established at closing of the sale in return for the release of the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;Claim and the release to the Company of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815194" contextRef="d_2023-04-01_2023-04-30_LitigationCaseAxis-EdwardsVacuumLlcWarrantyClaimMember_LitigationStatusAxis-SettledLitigationMember_LossContingenciesByNatureOfContingencyAxis-IndemnificationGuaranteeMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyReceivableProceeds" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">1.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million from a separate indemnification escrow.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company had been informed that Edwards sought recovery for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2020</em>&#160;Claim from the representation and warranty insurance Edwards obtained in connection with the closing of the sale of the semiconductor cryogenics business. During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">first</em>&#160;quarter of fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em>&#160;the Company was further informed that Edwards agreed to a payment under such insurance for claimed amounts more than the applicable indemnification deductibles established under the definitive agreement, but less than the total of claimed amounts submitted for recovery. Although management believes that any indemnifiable losses in excess of the applicable deductibles established in the definitive agreement would have been covered by such insurance, and the Company further disputes any liability under applicable law,&#160;Edwards is seeking recovery from the Company for claimed amounts purportedly&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;covered, or inadequately covered, by such insurance (the &#8220;Claim for Uncovered Amounts&#8221;).</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> September 12, 2025,&#160;</em>Edwards filed a lawsuit against the Company in the Supreme Court of the State of New York in the County of New York seeking indemnification from the Company under such definitive agreement seeking more than $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815209" contextRef="d_2025-09-12_2025-09-12_LitigationCaseAxis-Edwards2025ClaimMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyDamagesSoughtValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">13</ix:nonFraction> million, including attorney&#8217;s fees, arising from alleged breaches of representations and warranties relating to financial information provided by the Company in connection with the <em style="font: inherit;">2019</em> transaction (the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2025</em>&#160;Claim&#8221;). On <em style="font: inherit;"> October 21, 2025, </em>the Company filed a motion to dismiss the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Claim on the basis that all claims asserted in that action are time-barred. The Company&#8217;s motion to dismiss is pending as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 4, 2025. </em>The Company cannot determine the probability of any losses or outcome of the Claim for Uncovered Amounts including the amount of any indemnifiable losses, if any, resulting from the <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Claim. The Company, however, does&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;believe that this claim will have a material adverse effect on its consolidated financial position or results of operations, in each case, for continuing operations.&#160;Any potential expense incurred by the Company for these claims would be reflected in discontinued operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In the event of unexpected subsequent developments and given the inherent unpredictability of these matters, there can be&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;assurance that the Company&#8217;s assessment of these claims will reflect the ultimate outcome, and an adverse outcome in these matters could, from time to time, have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial position or results of operations in particular quarterly or annual periods.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3078623" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">4.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b>Business Combinations</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company recorded the assets acquired and liabilities assumed related to the following acquisitions at their fair values as of the acquisition date, from a market participant&#8217;s perspective. While the Company uses its best estimates and assumptions as part of the purchase price allocation process to value the assets acquired and liabilities assumed on the acquisition date, its estimates and assumptions are subject to refinement. Fair value estimates are based on a complex series of judgments about future events and uncertainties and rely heavily on estimates and assumptions. The judgments used to determine the estimated fair value assigned to each class of assets acquired and liabilities assumed, as well as asset lives, can materially impact the Company&#8217;s results of operations. The measurement period to finalize the fair values is completed within <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year after the respective acquisition date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><b>Ziath Ltd</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2, 2023, </em>the Company acquired Ziath, Ltd. and its subsidiaries (&#8220;Ziath&#8221;). Based in Cambridge, United Kingdom, Ziath is a leading provider of <em style="font: inherit;">2D</em> barcode readers for life science applications. Founded in <em style="font: inherit;">2005,</em> Ziath&#8217;s innovative <em style="font: inherit;">2D</em> barcode readers are a key component of the laboratory automation workflow serving pharmaceutical, biotechnology and academic customers worldwide. Ziath is expected to enhance the Company&#8217;s offerings, which support the entire lifecycle of sample management from specimen collection to sample registration, storage and processing. The acquisition was completed at a purchase price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815221" contextRef="d_2023-02-02_2023-02-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ZiathLtdMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">16.0</ix:nonFraction> million, net of cash acquired. The acquired business is included in the Sample Management Solutions&#160;segment.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The allocation of the consideration included $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815222" contextRef="i_2023-02-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ZiathLtdMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">12.0</ix:nonFraction> million of goodwill, $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815223" contextRef="d_2023-02-02_2023-02-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ZiathLtdMember_FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis-DevelopedTechnologyRightsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireBusinessesNetOfCashAcquired" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.1</ix:nonFraction> million of technology, $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815224" contextRef="i_2023-02-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ZiathLtdMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedDeferredTaxLiabilities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction> million of deferred tax liability, $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815225" contextRef="i_2023-02-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ZiathLtdMember_FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis-CustomerRelationshipsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedIntangibles" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.6</ix:nonFraction> million of customer relationships, $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815226" contextRef="i_2023-02-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ZiathLtdMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationRecognizedIdentifiableAssetsAcquiredAndLiabilitiesAssumedIntangibles" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction> million of trademarks, and several other assets and liabilities. The weighted average life of completed technology is <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2023-02-02_2023-02-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ZiathLtdMember_FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis-DevelopedTechnologyRightsMember" name="us-gaap:AcquiredFiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsWeightedAverageUsefulLife" id="c138815227" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years, customer relationships is <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2023-02-02_2023-02-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ZiathLtdMember_FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis-CustomerRelationshipsMember" name="us-gaap:AcquiredFiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsWeightedAverageUsefulLife" id="c138815228" format="ixt-sec:duryear">13</ix:nonNumeric> years, and trademarks is <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2023-02-02_2023-02-02_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-ZiathLtdMember_FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis-TrademarksMember" name="us-gaap:AcquiredFiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsWeightedAverageUsefulLife" id="c138815229" format="ixt-sec:duryear">13</ix:nonNumeric> years. The goodwill represents the Company&#8217;s ability to provide differentiated technology enabling high throughput scanning of varied formats of consumables. The goodwill is <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c138815230">not</span> expected to be deductible for income tax purposes.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> present pro forma financial information for its consolidated results of operations for the acquisition because such results are immaterial.</p>

   </ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Expected maturities could differ from contractual maturities because the security issuers <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have the right to prepay obligations without prepayment penalties.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Unrealized losses from fixed-income securities are primarily attributable to changes in interest rates. The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> believe any unrealized losses represent impairments based on the&#160;evaluation of the available evidence.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> February 1, 2023, </em>the Company entered into a&#160;cross-currency swap agreement to hedge the variability of exchange rate impacts between the U.S. dollar and the Euro. Under the terms of the cross-currency swap agreement, the Company notionally exchanged $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815263" contextRef="i_2025-02-03_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencySwap4Member_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">260.0</ix:nonFraction> million for&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c138815264">&#8364;250.0</span> million at a weighted average interest rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c138815265" contextRef="i_2025-02-03_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencySwap4Member_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DerivativeVariableInterestRate" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">1.80</ix:nonFraction>%. The Company designated the cross-currency swap as a hedge of net investments against <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of its Euro denominated subsidiaries, which requires an exchange of the notional amounts at maturity on <em style="font: inherit;"> February 2, 2026.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The cross-currency swaps were $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815267" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">33.4</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815268" contextRef="i_2024-09-30_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilities" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.9</ix:nonFraction> million and recorded within a&#160;&#8220;Derivative liability&#8221; as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025&#160;</em>and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2024, </em>respectively,&#160;in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 18pt;">
     The outstanding cross-currency swap&#160;is&#160;marked to market at each reporting period, representing the fair value&#160;of the cross-currency swap,&#160;any changes in fair value are recognized as a component of &#8220;Accumulated other comprehensive income (loss)&#8221; in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. The cross-currency swap is classified within Level
    <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> of the fair value hierarchy, described in Note
    <em style="font: inherit;">2,</em>&#160;
    <i>Summary of Significant Accounting Policies&#160;</i>and in&#160;Note
    <em style="font: inherit;">15,</em>&#160;
    <i style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Fair Value Measurements&#160;</i>below.
   </div>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Interest earned on the cross-currency swap is recorded within &#8220;Interest income, net&#8221; in the Consolidated Statements of Operations. For the fiscal years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, the Company recorded interest income&#160;of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815273" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeOther" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815274" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember_HedgingDesignationAxis-DesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:InterestIncomeOther" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.1</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively, on these instruments.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">8.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b>Goodwill and Intangible Assets </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Changes to the Company&#8217;s operating segments effective <em style="font: inherit;"> October 1, 2023 </em>resulted in a change to the Company&#8217;s reporting units, which are aligned to the Company&#8217;s operating and reportable segments (as further described in Note <em style="font: inherit;">18,</em> <i>Segment and Geographic Information</i> below). As a result of this segment realignment, the Company allocated goodwill to the reporting units existing under the new organizational structure on a relative fair value basis as of <em style="font: inherit;"> October 1, 2023. </em>The Company estimated the fair values of the affected businesses based upon the present value of their anticipated future cash flows. The Company's determination of fair value involved judgment and the use of significant estimates and assumptions. The Company&#160;tested its reporting units for potential impairment immediately before and after the segment realignment and concluded that the estimated fair value of each reporting unit exceeded its respective carrying value as of <em style="font: inherit;"> October 1, 2023.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company conducts an impairment assessment annually on&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> April 1,&#160;</em>or more frequently if impairment indicators are present. The Company determined that a&#160;sustained decline in its stock price&#160;was&#160;an indicator of potential impairment and performed&#160;an interim&#160;quantitative goodwill impairment test for its reporting units as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025. </em>The Company concluded that there was&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c138815293" contextRef="d_2025-04-01_2025-06-30_ReportingUnitAxis-SampleManagementSolutionsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction>&#160;impairment to goodwill for its Sample Management Solutions and Multiomics reporting units as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025.&#160;</em>Based on the results of the interim quantitative impairment test performed as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025,&#160;</em>the fair values of&#160;the Sample Management Solutions and Multiomics reporting units exceeded their respective carrying amounts.&#160;The Company concluded that there was <ix:nonFraction id="c138815294" contextRef="d_2025-04-01_2025-06-30_ReportingUnitAxis-SampleManagementSolutionsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction>&#160;impairment to goodwill for the Sample Management Solutions and Multiomics reporting units as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025.&#160;</em>The estimated fair value&#160;of each of the reporting units was derived based on the income approach and the market approach which were weighed at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">75%</em>&#160;and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">25%,</em>&#160;respectively, as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> June 30, 2025.&#160;</em>The DCF Method&#160;was used in the income approach which&#160;reflected the Company&#8217;s assumptions regarding revenue growth rates, forecasted gross profit margins, research and development expenses, selling, general and administrative expenses,&#160;capital expenditures, discount rates, terminal period growth rates, economic and market trends, and other expectations about the anticipated operating results of the Sample Management Solutions and Multiomics reporting units. The guideline company method was used in the market approach and publicly traded companies in similar lines of business were identified and used in an analysis to estimate the fair value. The Company qualitatively evaluated goodwill for impairment during the remainder of fiscal <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;and determined that there were&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;events or circumstances during the period to indicate an additional quantitative goodwill impairment assessment was required.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">9.</em> Restructuring</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt; text-indent: 9pt;"><b><i><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em></i></b>&#160;<b><i>Restructuring Plan</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em>&#160;quarter of fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em><i>,</i>&#160;the Company launched initiatives designed to optimize resources for future growth and improve efficiency across its organization. The focus of the initiatives is to improve the Company&#8217;s profitability, which includes facilities consolidation, portfolio optimization, and organization structure simplification. The Company expects to complete the activities included in these initiatives by the end of fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em><i>.</i>&#160;As of&#160;the date of issuance of the financial statements for the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025,&#160;</em>the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;identified restructuring actions related to these initiatives that will result in additional material charges. The Company expects to identify additional actions as it further refines its plan, and the&#160;related initiatives in future periods&#160;will be recorded when specified criteria are met, including but&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;limited to,&#160;communication of benefit arrangements or when the costs have been incurred.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The majority of the restructuring expenses associated with the initiatives described above for the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em> are severance and related costs.&#160;Of the total restructuring expenses in the fiscal year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025, </em>$<ix:nonFraction id="c138815321" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30_StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis-SampleManagementSolutionsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">2.0</ix:nonFraction> million is related to the Sample Management Solutions segment; $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815322" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30_StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis-MultiomicsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.1</ix:nonFraction> million is related to the Multiomics segment, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815323" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30_StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis-CorporateMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction> million is related to corporate.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The majority of the restructuring expenses associated with the initiatives described above for the fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2024&#160;</em>are severance and related costs, operating lease related ROU asset abandonment, and fixed assets and other asset write-offs. Of the total restructuring expenses in the fiscal year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2024,&#160;</em>$<ix:nonFraction id="c138815324" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30_StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis-SampleManagementSolutionsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million is related to the Sample Management Solutions&#160;segment and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815325" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30_StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis-CorporateMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringCharges" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">3.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million is the Company&#8217;s headquarters operating lease related ROU asset abandonment and corporate related severance costs.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><b><i><em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> Cost Savings Plan</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> quarters of fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> the Company announced cost savings plans designed to position the Company to meet the needs of its&#160;customers and accelerate growth of the business.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The majority of the restructuring expenses for fiscal years <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>&#160;are related to severance and related costs. The cost savings plans were completed and costs from the actions were fully realized by the end of the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em>&#160;&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Contract Balances</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Accounts Receivable, Net. </i>Accounts receivable represent rights to consideration in exchange for products or services that have been transferred by the Company, when payment is unconditional and only the passage of time is required before payment is due. Accounts receivable do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> bear interest and are recorded at the invoiced amount. The Company maintains an allowance for expected credit losses representing its best estimate of probable credit losses related to its existing accounts receivable and their net realizable value. The Company determines the allowance for expected credit losses based on a number of factors, including an evaluation of customer credit worthiness, the age of the outstanding receivables, economic trends, historical experience, and other information through the payment periods. Accounts receivable, net were $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815398" contextRef="i_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccountsReceivableNetCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">142.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815399" contextRef="i_2024-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccountsReceivableNetCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">154.2</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Contract Assets. </i>Contract assets represent rights to consideration in exchange for products or services that have been transferred by the Company, when payment is conditional on something other than the passage of time. These amounts typically relate to contracts where the right to invoice the customer is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> present until completion of the contract or the achievement of specified milestones and the value of the products or services transferred exceed this constraint. Contract assets are classified as current as they are expected to convert to cash within <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year. Contract asset balances which are included within &#8220;Prepaid expenses and other current assets&#8221; on the Consolidated Balance Sheet, were $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815403" contextRef="i_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerAssetNetCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">37.3</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815404" contextRef="i_2024-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerAssetNetCurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">28.9</ix:nonFraction> million at <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively. Revenue of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815406" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="azta:ContractWithCustomerAssetRevenueRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">30.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million recognized during the year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em>&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815407" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="azta:ContractWithCustomerAssetRevenueRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">18.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million recognized during the year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2024</em>&#160;contributed to the contract asset&#160;balances at <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><i>Contract Liabilities. </i>Contract liabilities represent the Company&#8217;s obligation to transfer products or services to a customer for which consideration has been received, or for which an amount of consideration is due from the customer. Contract assets and liabilities are reported on a net basis at the contract level, depending on the contracts position at the end of each reporting period. Contract liabilities are included within &#8220;Deferred revenue&#8221; on the Consolidated Balance Sheet. Contract liabilities were $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815409" contextRef="i_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiability" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">34.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million,&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c138815410" contextRef="i_2024-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiability" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">30.5</ix:nonFraction> million, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815411" contextRef="d_2022-10-01_2023-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityRevenueRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">34.2</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;at fiscal years ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, respectively. Revenue recognized from the contract liability balance at <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2023 </em>was $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815414" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityRevenueRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">27.8</ix:nonFraction> million for the year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2024</em>, and revenue recognized from the contract liability balance at <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2024</em>&#160;was $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815415" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ContractWithCustomerLiabilityRevenueRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">18.4</ix:nonFraction> million for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em>.</p>
