   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;text-align:justify;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Cost to Obtain and Fulfill a Contract</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company capitalizes sales commissions when incurred if they are (i) incremental costs of obtaining a contract, (ii) expected to be recovered and (iii) have an expected amortization period that is greater than <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year. These amounts primarily relate to sales commissions and are being amortized over a <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-09-30" name="us-gaap:CapitalizedContractCostAmortizationPeriod" id="c138815420" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">60</ix:nonNumeric>-month period, which represents the average period of contract performance. The&#160;capitalized&#160;sales commissions&#160;were&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c138815421" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CapitalizedContractCostAmortization" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815422" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:CapitalizedContractCostAmortization" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million at&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>,&#160;respectively. All other sales commissions incurred during the reporting period have been expensed as incurred. These costs are recorded within &#8220;Selling, general and administrative&#8221; expenses on the Consolidated Statement of Operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company accounts for shipping and handling activities as fulfillment activities and recognize the associated expense when control of the product has transferred to the customer.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">14.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b>Stock Based Compensation</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In accordance with the <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> Equity Incentive Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2020</em> Plan&#8221;), the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue eligible employees options to purchase shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock, restricted stock units&#160;and other equity incentives, which vest upon the satisfaction of a performance condition and/or a service condition. In addition, the Company issues common stock to participating employees pursuant to an employee stock purchase plan, and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>issue&#160;common stock awards and deferred restricted stock units to members of its Board of Directors in accordance with its Board of Directors compensation program.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i><em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> Equity Incentive Plan </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">In accordance with the <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> Plan, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>grant employees (i)&#160;restricted stock and other stock-based awards, (ii)&#160;nonqualified stock options, and (iii)&#160;options intended to qualify as incentive stock options under Section&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">422</em> of the Internal Revenue Code. All employees of the Company or any affiliate of the Company, independent directors, consultants and advisors are eligible to participate in the <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> Plan. The <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> Plan provides for the issuance of an aggregate of <ix:nonFraction id="c138815432" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_PlanNameAxis-EquityIncentivePlan2020Member" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,800,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of common stock, including <ix:nonFraction id="c138815433" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_PlanNameAxis-EquityIncentivePlan2020Member" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,500,000</ix:nonFraction> shares reserved for issuance pursuant to the <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> Plan, and up to <ix:nonFraction id="c138815435" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_PlanNameAxis-EquityIncentivePlan2020Member" unitRef="USD" name="azta:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorizedAwardsForfeitedExpiredOrCanceledUnderOtherPlans" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">300,000</ix:nonFraction> additional shares which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be issued pursuant to the <em style="font: inherit;">2020</em> Plan if outstanding awards granted under the Company&#8217;s previous <em style="font: inherit;">2000</em> Plan or the Company&#8217;s previous&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2015</em> Plan are forfeited, expire or are cancelled.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Time-Based Restricted Stock Unit Grants </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Restricted stock units granted with a required service period typically have <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c138815459">three</span>-year vesting schedules in which <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c138815460">one</span>-<em style="font: inherit;">third</em> of awards vest at each annual anniversary of grant date, subject to the award holders meeting service requirements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Performance-Based Restricted Stock Unit Grants</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Performance-based restricted stock units are earned based on the achievement of performance criteria established by the Human Resources and Compensation Committee and approved by the Board of Directors. The criteria for performance-based awards are weighted and have threshold, target and maximum performance goals.&#160;Performance-based restricted stock units <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>also have a required service period following the achievement of all or a portion of the performance goals.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> October 2023,&#160;</em>the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approved an amendment to the performance goals associated with the previously issued performance-based restricted stock units for all impacted employees, excluding members of the Company&#8217;s executive team. The performance goals, as amended, were&#160;more reflective of the then current macroeconomic environment and consideration toward employee retention in the competitive life sciences industry. Before the amendment, the original performance goals were&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;expected to be satisfied. Subsequent to the amendment, vesting became probable based on the forecasted achievement of the amended performance goals. The amendment of these restricted stock units is treated as a modification with the total potential maximum compensation cost of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815464" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EmployeeServiceShareBasedCompensationNonvestedAwardsTotalCompensationCostNotYetRecognized" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">3.0</ix:nonFraction> million recognized over the service period through&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2025.&#160;</em>The Company recorded expense of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815465" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardPlanModificationIncrementalCompensationCost" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">1.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million during the fiscal&#160;year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025&#160;</em>related to the modified awards.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">These performance-based restricted stock unit awards granted allow participants to earn <ix:nonFraction id="c138815466" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="azta:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardPerformanceAwardsPercentageEarnedIfGoalsMet" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of restricted stock units if the Company&#8217;s performance meets or exceeds its target goal for each applicable financial metric, and up to a maximum of <ix:nonFraction id="c138815467" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30_AwardTypeAxis-PerformanceBasedRestrictedStockUnitsMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" unitRef="Pure" name="azta:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardPerformanceAwardsPercentageEarnedIfGoalsMet" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">200</ix:nonFraction>% if the Company&#8217;s performance for such metrics meets or exceeds the maximum or stretch goal. Performance below the minimum threshold for each financial metric results in award forfeiture. Performance goals are measured over a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c138815468">three</span>-year period for each year&#8217;s restricted stock unit awards and at the end of the period to determine the number of restricted stock units earned, if any, by recipients who continue to meet the service requirement. Upon the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> anniversary of each year&#8217;s restricted stock unit awards&#8217; grant date, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors approves&#160;the number of restricted stock units earned for participants who continue to meet the service requirements on the vest date. For restricted stock unit awards that include vesting based on performance conditions, the fair values are estimated based on the intrinsic values of the awards at the grant date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024</em><i>,</i>&#160;the Company issued restricted stock unit awards with vesting based on market conditions, which will vest based on achievement of the Company's&#160;relative total shareholder return against the defined peer group&#160;over a&#160;<span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c138815470">three</span>-year period. The fair values for those grants that include vesting based on market conditions are estimated using the Monte Carlo simulation model.&#160;The key assumptions used in the Monte Carlo simulation included (i) the expected volatility of <ix:nonFraction id="c138815471" contextRef="d_2024-11-01_2024-11-30_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsExpectedVolatilityRateMinimum" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">49.3</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction id="c138815472" contextRef="d_2024-11-01_2024-11-30_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsExpectedVolatilityRateMaximum" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">50.3</ix:nonFraction>% based on the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year daily historical volatility as measured on the grant date, (ii) risk-free interest rate of <ix:nonFraction id="c138815474" contextRef="d_2024-11-01_2024-11-30_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsRiskFreeInterestRateMinimum" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">3.96</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction id="c138815475" contextRef="d_2024-11-01_2024-11-30_AwardTypeAxis-RestrictedStockUnitsRSUMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsRiskFreeInterestRateMaximum" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">4.27</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;based on U.S. Treasury constant maturities yields&#160;as of the grant date, (iii) correlation assumption based on daily share price changes over&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;years between the Company and the peer companies measured on the grant date, and (iv)&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;expected dividend yield.&#160;The compensation cost is recognized ratably over the requisite service period for those grants, which will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be reversed solely because the market condition is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> satisfied.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Awards Granted to the Board of Directors</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The stock-based compensation granted to members of the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors includes Company&#160;shares or restricted stock units.&#160;Non-employee directors <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>elect to defer receipt of their stock compensation in exchange for a credit, in restricted stock units, to a deferred restricted stock unit (&#8220;deferred RSU&#8221;) account.&#160;Directors who make a deferral election will have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> rights as stockholders of the Company with respect to amounts credited to their deferred RSU account. The restricted stock units credited to the deferred RSU account will be released at the time specified in the director&#8217;s deferral election, but <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> later than as soon as administratively feasible following the date the director reaches age <em style="font: inherit;">65</em> or the director&#8217;s termination of Board service. Certain&#160;members of&#160;the Board of Directors have elected to defer receipt of their&#160;stock compensation and received a credit of restricted stock units in their&#160;deferred RSU&#160;account and the total number of deferred stock awards held by the non-employee directors&#160;was <ix:nonFraction id="c138815483" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_AwardTypeAxis-DeferredStockAwardsMember_TitleOfIndividualAxis-DirectorMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsNonvestedNumber" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">26,079</ix:nonFraction> as of <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Employee Stock Purchase Plan</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company maintains an employee stock purchase plan that allows its employees to purchase shares of common stock at a price equal to <ix:nonFraction id="c138815484" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30_PlanNameAxis-EmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardPurchasePriceOfCommonStockPercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">85</ix:nonFraction>% of the fair market value of the Company&#8217;s stock at the beginning or the end of the semi-annual offering period, whichever is lower. On <em style="font: inherit;"> February&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">8,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2017,</em> the stockholders approved the <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> Employee Stock Purchase Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2017</em> Plan&#8221;). The <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> Plan allows for purchases by employees of up to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c138815490" contextRef="i_2024-09-30_PlanNameAxis-EmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAuthorized" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,250,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em>, <ix:nonFraction id="c138815491" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_PlanNameAxis-EmployeeStockPurchasePlanMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">436,369</ix:nonFraction> shares of common stock remain available for purchase under the <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> Plan. During the fiscal years&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction id="c138815495" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesEmployeeStockPurchasePlans" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">77,265</ix:nonFraction> shares, <ix:nonFraction id="c138815496" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesEmployeeStockPurchasePlans" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">72,787</ix:nonFraction> shares, and <ix:nonFraction id="c138815497" contextRef="d_2022-10-01_2023-09-30" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesEmployeeStockPurchasePlans" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">83,715</ix:nonFraction> shares respectively, under the <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> Plan.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The risk-free rate is based on the U.S.&#160;Treasury yield curve for notes with terms approximating the expected life of the shares granted. The expected stock price volatility is determined based on the Company&#8217;s historic stock prices over a period commensurate with the expected life of the shares granted. The expected life represents the weighted average period over which the shares are expected to be purchased. Dividend yields are projected based on the Company&#8217;s history of dividend declarations and management&#8217;s intention for future dividend declarations.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Cash Equivalents</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Cash equivalents consisting of money market funds are classified within Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> of the fair value hierarchy because they are valued using quoted market prices in active markets. Cash equivalents consisting of&#160;certificates of deposit are&#160;classified within&#160;Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> of the fair value hierarchy because they are&#160;valued using observable market inputs, <em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;active market prices.&#160;The Company considers all highly liquid interest-earning investments with a maturity of <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months or less at the date of purchase to be cash equivalents. The fair values of these investments approximate their carrying values.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Available-For-Sale Securities</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Available-for-sale securities primarily consist of highly rated corporate debt securities and U.S. government backed securities which are classified as Level <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> Investments classified as Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> consist of debt securities that are valued using matrix pricing and benchmarking because they are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> actively traded, and bank certificates of deposit. Matrix pricing is a mathematical technique used to value securities by relying on the securities&#8217; relationship to other benchmark quoted prices.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;"><i><b>Convertible Debt Securities and&#160;Investment in Equity Securities</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>&#160;quarter of fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em><i>,</i>&#160;the Company purchased $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815515" contextRef="d_2024-04-01_2024-06-30_FinancialInstrumentAxis-ConvertibleDebtSecuritiesMember_InvestmentIssuerNameAxis-PrivateCompanyMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireEquitySecuritiesFvNi" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">2.0</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million principal amount of convertible notes issued by a private company. The Company accounted for the investment in these convertible notes at fair value with changes in fair value recognized in the&#160;Consolidated Statement of Operations. As of the conversion of these notes into preferred stock of the private company described below, the fair value of the convertible notes was $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815516" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_InvestmentIssuerNameAxis-PrivateCompanyMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ConvertibleDebtFairValueDisclosures" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">first</em>&#160;quarter of fiscal year&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em><i>,</i>&#160;the Company converted the&#160;convertible notes&#160;into&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c138815519" contextRef="d_2024-10-02_2024-10-02_DebtConversionByUniqueDescriptionAxis-ConversionFromConvertibleNotesToPreferredStockPrincipalAndInterestMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:DebtConversionConvertedInstrumentSharesIssued1" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">420,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares of preferred stock of the private company. The conversion did&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;result in the recognition of additional gain or loss on the convertible notes. The shares of preferred stock are equity securities and within the scope of ASC&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">321,</em></i>&#160;<i>Investments - Equity Securities</i>. The Company elected the measurement alternative for its investment in the shares of preferred stock&#160;because the shares&#160;do&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">not</em>&#160;have a readily determinable fair value. As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025, </em>the carrying value of the investment in the shares of preferred stock&#160;was $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815523" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_FinancialInstrumentAxis-ConvertibleDebtSecuritiesMember_InvestmentIssuerNameAxis-PrivateCompanyMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:EquitySecuritiesFvNiCurrentAndNoncurrent" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">2.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and is included in &#8220;Other assets&#8221; on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. The fair value determination is classified as Level&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">3</em></i>&#160;based on unobservable inputs which were based on the best information available in the circumstance, including transaction pricing, recent acquisition, and market participant assumptions. The unobservable inputs used in the determination of the fair value of assets classified as Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>&#160;have an inherent measurement uncertainty that if changed could result in higher or lower fair value measurements of the assets as of the reporting date.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><i>Foreign Exchange Contracts &amp; Net Investment Hedge </i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company's foreign exchange contract assets and liabilities, and its&#160;net investment hedge assets and liabilities&#160;are measured and reported at fair value using the market method valuation technique. The inputs to this technique utilize current foreign currency exchange forward market rates published by <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party leading financial news and data providers. These are observable data that represent the rates that the financial institution uses for contracts entered into at that date; however, they are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> based on actual transactions, so they are classified as Level <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em>&#160;<b> </b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><b><i>Assets and Liabilities Measured at Fair Value on a Nonrecurring Basis</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In addition to assets and liabilities that are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis, impairment indicators&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> may&#160;</em>subject goodwill and long-lived assets to fair value measurement on a nonrecurring basis. As described in Note <em style="font: inherit;">8</em><i>,</i>&#160;<i>Goodwill and Intangible Assets,</i>&#160;the Company&#160;concluded that there was <ix:nonFraction id="c138815530" contextRef="d_2024-10-01_2025-09-30_FairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis-FairValueMeasurementsNonrecurringMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AssetImpairmentCharges" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction>&#160;impairment to goodwill for its Sample Management Solutions and Multiomics reporting units during fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em>&#160;During the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em>&#160;quarter of fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em><i>,</i>&#160;the Company discontinued its sample sourcing product offering (a product line within the Sample Management Solutions&#160;segment). As a result, the Company recorded a $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815535" contextRef="d_2023-10-01_2024-09-30_ReportingUnitAxis-SampleManagementSolutionsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million impairment of intangible assets related to the sample sourcing business within&#160;&#8220;Impairment of goodwill and intangible assets&#8221; in its Consolidated Statements of Operations during&#160;the fiscal year&#160;ended <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2024.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> provided deferred income taxes on the outside basis differences of any other foreign subsidiary and maintains its general assertion of indefinite reinvestment regarding those subsidiaries and the remaining earnings of its China subsidiary as of <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em>. The remaining foreign earnings total approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815560" contextRef="i_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:UndistributedEarningsOfForeignSubsidiaries" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">377.5</ix:nonFraction> million as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em> and are expected to be reinvested in foreign operations and acquisitions. The Company did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> calculate estimated deferred tax liabilities on the remaining earnings because such calculations would <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be practicable due to the complexity of its hypothetical calculation. The taxes on these earnings would primarily consist of foreign withholding taxes, taxes on foreign exchange gains and losses resulting from potential future distributions, and U.S. state income taxes. Substantially all of the unremitted earnings of the Company have been federally taxed in the United States&#160;based on the international tax regulations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The global minimum tax of <em style="font: inherit;">fifteen</em> percent under the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development&#8217;s (&#8220;OECD&#8221;) Pillar Two Global Anti-Base Erosion Rule is currently effective in certain jurisdictions in which we operate.&#160;The OECD continues to issue guidance on the framework and various countries continue to enact legislation with respect to their application of the framework.&#160;The Company has considered these rules in effect in the countries in which it operates and there is currently <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> impact to its&#160;financial statements.&#160; The rules are being monitored closely in the United States&#160;and the Company expects to be below the revenue threshold.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 4, 2025, </em>the &#8220;One Big Beautiful Bill Act&#8221; was signed into U.S. tax law, extending many international provisions of the <em style="font: inherit;">2017</em> Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and providing additional favorable incentives.&#160; The Company will continue to monitor the financial impact of these changes. In the near term, the Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect these changes to have an impact on the effective tax rate or cash flows. Many of the key incentives are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> initially being elected by the Company.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The deferred tax assets on the balance sheets for <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> also include $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815571" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_TypeOfArrangementAxis-IntercompanyProfitEliminationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredIncomeTaxAssetsNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815572" contextRef="i_2024-09-30_TypeOfArrangementAxis-IntercompanyProfitEliminationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredIncomeTaxAssetsNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.6</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million deferred tax charges related to the company&#8217;s intercompany profit elimination, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740,</em> <i>Income Taxes</i>, requires that all available evidence, both positive and negative, be considered in determining, based on the weight of that evidence, whether a valuation allowance is needed. The weight given to the potential effect of negative and positive evidence should be commensurate with the extent to which it can be objectively verified. The more negative evidence that exists, (a)&#160;the more positive evidence is necessary and (b)&#160;the more difficult it is to support a conclusion that a valuation allowance is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> needed for some portion or the entire deferred tax asset.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company evaluates the realizability of its deferred tax assets and assesses the need for a valuation allowance on a quarterly basis. The Company operates in numerous countries under many legal forms and, as a result, is subject to the jurisdiction of numerous domestic and foreign tax authorities. The Company&#160;evaluates the profitability of its&#160;operations in each jurisdiction on a historic cumulative basis and on a forward-looking basis, while carefully considering carry-forward periods of tax attributes&#160;and ongoing tax planning strategies in assessing the need for the valuation allowance.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company maintains valuation allowances of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815575" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">27.9</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million against&#160;deferred tax assets in the United States as of <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025. </em>The Company also maintains valuation allowances against net deferred tax assets in certain foreign jurisdictions totaling $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815576" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-ForeignCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">74.1</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025.&#160;</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025</em>, the Company has tax-effected federal, state and foreign&#160;loss carry-forwards of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815577" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-DomesticCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.4</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million, $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815578" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-StateAndLocalJurisdictionMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">7.4</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815579" contextRef="i_2025-09-30_IncomeTaxAuthorityAxis-ForeignCountryMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">74.9</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively. The federal net operating losses carry forward indefinitely with the deductions limited to <em style="font: inherit;">eighty</em> percent of taxable income in any given year. The state net operating loss carry-forwards will begin to expire in <em style="font: inherit;">2033.</em> Many of the foreign net operating loss carry-forwards have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> limit in number of years, but some have&#160;deductions capped at a certain percent of taxable income.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The Company has performed studies to determine if there are any annual limitations on the federal net operating losses under Section <em style="font: inherit;">382</em> of the Internal Revenue Code of <em style="font: inherit;">1986,</em> as amended, or the Internal Revenue Code. As a result of these studies, the Company has determined that ownership changes occurred primarily in connection with acquired subsidiaries.&#160; The benefits of the net operating losses that will expire before utilization have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been recorded as deferred tax assets in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.&#160; Subsequent ownership changes <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>further affect the limitation in future years.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company maintains liabilities for unrecognized tax benefits.    <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company is subject to U.S.&#160;federal, state, local and foreign income taxes in various jurisdictions.    <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">In the normal course of business, the Company is subject to income tax audits in various global jurisdictions in which it operates. The&#160;years subject to examination vary for the United States&#160;and international jurisdictions, with the earliest tax&#160;year being <em style="font: inherit;">2019.</em> Based on the outcome of these examinations or the expiration of statutes of limitations for specific jurisdictions, it is reasonably possible that the related unrecognized tax benefits could change from those recorded in the Consolidated Balance Sheets. In fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> the Company recognized tax benefits of $<ix:nonFraction id="c138815590" contextRef="i_2025-09-30" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DecreaseInUnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIsReasonablyPossible" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">0.3</ix:nonFraction> million due to statute of limitations expirations.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">18.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b>Segment and Geographic Information </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Operating segments are defined as components of an enterprise that engage in business activities&#160;from which it <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>recognize revenues and incur expenses, and for which discrete financial information is available and regularly reviewed by the CODM&#160;in deciding how to allocate resources and to assess performance. The Company&#8217;s operations are organized and managed by type of products and services and segment information is reported accordingly. The Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer is the Company&#8217;s CODM. There have been <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> operating segments aggregated to arrive at the Company&#8217;s reportable segments. Revenues for all operating segments include only transactions with unaffiliated customers and include <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> intersegment revenues. The accounting policies of the reportable segments are the same as those described in Note <em style="font: inherit;">2,</em> <i>Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</i>.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 12, 2024</em><i>,</i>&#160;the Company&#8217;s B Medical Systems business&#160;met the &#8220;held for sale&#8221; criteria and &#8220;discontinued operations&#8221; criteria in accordance with FASB ASC&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">205</em></i>&#160;and the results of the B Medical Systems business&#160;are included within discontinued operations. As a result, the Company&#8217;s continuing operations includes the following <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c138815602">two</span> operating and reportable segments:</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;width:100%;margin-left:auto;margin-right:auto;"><tbody><tr><td style="vertical-align:top;width:4%;">&#160;</td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:4%;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;width:auto;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Sample Management Solutions</b>. The Multiomics business resources operate as&#160;a single business unit offering genomic and other sample analysis services, including gene sequencing, synthesis and related services.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Management considers adjusted operating income (loss) as the primary performance metric when evaluating each&#160;segment&#8217;s operations. The Company uses this measure because it helps management understand and evaluate the segments&#8217; core operating results and facilitates comparison of performance for determining compensation.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The CODM uses segment revenues and segment adjusted operating income (loss) predominantly in the monthly and quarterly business review processes. During these processes, the CODM considers budget-to-actual variances to evaluate both internal (for example, changes in selling prices, strategic growth investments, productivity and&#160;business mix) and external (for example, inflation and&#160;foreign currency) events and conditions.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size:8pt;">(<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)</span></p> </td><td style="width: auto;"> <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 8pt; text-align: justify;">Transformation costs represent non-recurring expenses for strategic projects with anticipated long-term benefits to the Company focused on cost reduction and productivity improvement that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the definition of restructuring charges. These costs are directed at simplifying, standardizing, streamlining, and optimizing the Company&#8217;s operations, processes and systems to permanently alter the Company&#8217;s operations for the long term. For a project to be considered transformational, successful completion of the project must be expected to bring long-term material benefits to the organization and involve significant changes to process and/or underlying technology. Transformation costs in the period result from actions taken as part of the Company&#8217;s <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em> transformation&#160;plan&#160;and primarily relate to <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> time asset write downs associated with changes in technology, <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> time inventory write downs relating to restructuring actions taken in the period, and <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party consulting costs associated with process and&#160;systems re-design.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Adjusted operating income (loss) excludes charges related to amortization of intangible assets, transformation costs, restructuring charges, goodwill and intangible asset impairment,&#160;merger and acquisition costs,&#160;costs related to share repurchase and&#160;governance-related matters, and other miscellaneous expenses.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The segment expenses regularly provided to the CODM are adjusted cost of revenues which primarily consist of costs of direct materials and direct labor, freight, warranty, depreciation expenses, and facilities costs&#160;and adjusted operating expenses which&#160;primarily consists of employee salaries and benefits for R&amp;D, selling, marketing, and administrative personnel, commissions, advertising and promotional expenses, audit, legal and strategic consulting fees, depreciation expenses, facilities costs, insurance, and information systems costs. Centrally incurred costs are primarily allocated to segments using a percentage of budgeted segment revenue over total revenue.</p>

   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">19.</em></b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b>Commitments and Contingencies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;"><b><i>Contingencies</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">The Company is subject to various legal proceedings, both asserted and unasserted, that arise in the ordinary course of business. The Company cannot predict the ultimate outcome of such legal proceedings or, in certain instances, provide reasonable ranges of potential losses.&#160;The Company&#160;considers all claims on a quarterly basis and based on known facts assesses whether potential losses are considered reasonably possible, probable, and estimable. Based upon this assessment, the Company&#160;then evaluates disclosure requirements and whether to accrue for such claims in the consolidated financial statements.&#160;At&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 30, 2025&#160;</em>and as of the date of issuance&#160;of these consolidated financial statements, the Company&#160;believes that&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;new material provision for liability nor new disclosure is required related to any claims.&#160;In the event of unexpected subsequent developments and given the inherent unpredictability of these matters, there can be&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em>&#160;assurance that the Company&#8217;s assessment of any claim will reflect the ultimate outcome, and an adverse outcome in certain matters could, from time to time, have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial position or results of operations in particular quarterly or annual periods.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b><a id="controls" title="controls" href="#"></a>Item</b>&#160;<b>9A.</b>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;<b><i>Controls and Procedures</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, we conducted an evaluation of our disclosure controls and procedures, as such term is defined under Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) promulgated under the Exchange Act. Disclosure controls and procedures are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and forms and that such information is accumulated and communicated to management, including the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. Based upon this evaluation, our Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of September 30, 2025, the end of the period covered by this Annual Report on Form 10-K due to the material weaknesses described below. Notwithstanding the material weaknesses and based on additional analyses and other procedures management performed, our Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Financial Officer have concluded that the&#160;consolidated financial statements included in this Annual&#160;Report on Form 10-K&#160;are fairly stated in all material respects in accordance with U.S. GAAP for each of the periods presented.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Management</b>&#8217;<b>s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting. Internal control over financial reporting is defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act, as a process designed by, or under the supervision of our Chief Executive and Chief Financial Officers and effected by our board of directors, management and other personnel to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with U.S. GAAP and includes those policies and procedures that:</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">

     <td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td>

     <td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">pertain to the maintenance of records that in reasonable detail accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and disposition of our assets;</p> </td>
    </tr>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Because of its inherent limitations, internal control over financial reporting may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risks that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, we conducted an assessment of the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of September 30, 2025. In making this assessment, we used the criteria set forth in <i>Internal Control - Integrated Framework</i> (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations (COSO) of the Treadway Commission. Based on this evaluation, management concluded that, as of&#160;September 30, 2025, our&#160;internal control over financial reporting was not effective due to the material weaknesses described below.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">A material weakness is a deficiency, or combination of deficiencies, in internal control over financial reporting, such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of a company&#8217;s annual or interim consolidated financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis. The following material weaknesses were identified as of September 30, 2025:</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <div class="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">

     <td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">As initially disclosed in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended September 30, 2024, we did not design and maintain effective controls related to the review of the cash flow statement. This&#160;material weakness resulted in immaterial misstatements in our Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for the Q2 and Q3 interim periods during fiscal year 2023, the year ended September 30, 2023, the Q1, Q2, and Q3 interim periods&#160;during fiscal year 2024, the Q1&#160;interim period&#160;during fiscal year 2025,&#160;and in our supplemental cash flow disclosures for the year ended September 30, 2022, each interim and annual period during fiscal year 2023 and the Q1, Q2 and Q3 interim periods during fiscal year 2024.</p> </td>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">Additionally, these material weaknesses&#160;could result in misstatements of substantially all account balances and disclosures that would result in a material misstatement to our interim or annual consolidated financial statements that would not be prevented or detected on a timely basis.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">The effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of&#160;September 30, 2025&#160;has been audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, an independent registered public accounting firm, as stated in their report which appears in Part II, Item 8, &#8220;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data&#8221; of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -19pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><b>Remediation Plans</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Statements of Cash Flows</i>&#160;&#8211; During fiscal 2025, management has continued to take steps to remediate the material weakness, including implementing&#160;a new cash flow reporting tool which automates the calculation of the effect of exchange rate changes on cash and cash equivalents.&#160; In addition, we implemented&#160;and documented&#160;new processes and controls over the review of the consolidated statement of&#160;cash flows.&#160;&#160;While the new and enhanced controls have been designed and implemented and we monitored and evaluated their effectiveness during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, they have not operated for a sufficient period&#160;as of September&#160;30, 2025&#160;to assert the material weakness has been remediated.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Account Reconciliations</i>&#160;&#8211; Since the identification of the material weakness in the fiscal second quarter of 2025, including during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, we have started taking the necessary steps to work towards remediating the material weakness. Specifically, we are designing and enhancing the controls and precision level over balance sheet reconciliations, drafting a new policy, and working with outside consultants to assist in certain aspects of the remediation plan. We will continue to take the necessary steps to address this material weakness.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;"><i>Expense Classification</i> &#8211; Management is in the process of designing and implementing the remediation plan to address the material weakness.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 18pt;">These&#160;material weaknesses will not be considered remediated until we have completed the design and implementation of the applicable controls and they operate for a sufficient period&#160;for management to&#160;conclude, through testing, that such controls are operating effectively.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 18pt;">We are committed to continuing to improve our internal control over financial reporting, and as we continue to evaluate and work to improve our internal control over financial reporting, we may take additional measures to address control deficiencies, or we may modify certain of the remediation measures described above.</p>
  <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 7pt;text-indent:18pt;">&#160;</p>
